title: Free Samples Steal $1,800/Year Using Your Brain
hook: Every free sample you've ever accepted was engineered to trigger a specific brain response — and it's costing the average family $1,800 a year.
angle: The Reciprocity Principle as a deliberate retail weapon: stores scientifically exploit the human obligation reflex to generate unplanned purchases. Costco sample stations boost purchase rates 300%. Most people never connect the sample to the spending.
audience: Anyone who shops at Costco, grocery stores, wine stores, or food courts — basically every consumer
key_numbers: 300% purchase rate boost from sample stations
$1,800/year average unplanned spending triggered by free samples
$47 average impulse purchase following a free taste
Robert Cialdini documented the reciprocity effect in 1984 — retailers have been deploying it since
